factual_claims.source_evidence: Note 10: Basic and diluted EPS for 2026 is EUR 0.02 vs EUR 0.04 for 2025.

factual_claims.claim: The weaker results reflected a 24.0% increase in operating expenses to EUR 20.2 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Note 12: Total operating expenses for 2026 were EUR 20,184 thousand (20.184M), a 24.0% increase from EUR 16,277 thousand (16.277M) in 2025.

factual_claims.claim: Fuel costs rose 47.6% to EUR 4.4 million because of higher diesel prices and more severe ice conditions, which increased ferry fuel consumption.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Note 12: Fuel costs increased from EUR 2,969 thousand (2025) to EUR 4,382 thousand (2026), a 47.6% increase. Management Report attributes this to 'higher diesel prices' and 'more severe ice conditions.'

factual_claims.claim: Electricity costs increased 28.8% to EUR 3.1 million, partly due to higher market and network-service prices and a new security-of-supply fee.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Note 12: Electricity costs rose from EUR 2,403 thousand (2025) to EUR 3,096 thousand (2026), a 28.8% increase. Management Report cites 'higher electricity and network service prices' and 'the security of supply fee introduced at the beginning of the year.'

factual_claims.claim: Technical maintenance and repair costs rose 80.0% to EUR 2.8 million, including more extensive repairs to Botnica, ferries, and harbour infrastructure.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Note 12: Technical maintenance and repair costs increased from EUR 1,547 thousand (2025) to EUR 2,784 thousand (2026), an 80.0% increase. Management Report details repairs to 'the icebreaker Botnica, the quays in the Old City Harbour and the ferries.'

factual_claims.claim: Depreciation, amortisation and impairment increased 6.0% to EUR 12.9 million, mainly following the commissioning of the Paldiski South Harbour quay, capitalised ferry dry-docking projects, and impairments of old engines.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Note 12: Depreciation, amortisation and impairment increased from EUR 12,140 thousand (2025) to EUR 12,867 thousand (2026), a 6.0% increase. Management Report attributes this to 'the commissioning of the new quay at Paldiski South Harbour and the capitalisation of several ferry dry-docking projects... and the impairment of old engines.'

factual_claims.claim: Operating volumes were also weaker.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management Report: 'Cargo volumes decreased by 0.3 million tonnes (–5.0%) in the 6 months... The number of passengers fell by 2.0% (–73 thousand passengers).'

factual_claims.claim: Cargo volumes fell 5.0% to 6.5 million tonnes, primarily because liquid bulk decreased 33.8%; dry bulk declined 4.8%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating Volumes section: 'In the first 6 months of 2026, the Group’s harbours handled a total of 6.5 million tonnes of cargo, a decrease of 0.3 million tonnes (–5.0%). The decline was mainly attributable to a decrease in liquid bulk volumes, which fell by 0.3 million tonnes (–33.8%). Dry bulk volumes also declined by 58 thousand tonnes (–4.8%).'

factual_claims.claim: Passenger numbers fell 2.0% to 3.6 million, with lower traffic on the Tallinn–Helsinki and Tallinn–Stockholm routes.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating Volumes section: 'In the first 6 months of 2026, the number of passengers decreased by 73 thousand to 3.6 million (–2.0%). The largest decline was recorded on the Tallinn–Helsinki route... and Tallinn–Stockholm route.'

factual_claims.claim: The Tallinn–Helsinki decline was partly linked to the scheduled dry-docking of the vessel Finlandia.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating Volumes section: 'The largest decline was recorded on the Tallinn–Helsinki route, where passenger numbers fell by 85 thousand (– 2.6%), mainly due to the scheduled dry-docking of Eckerö Line’s vessel Finlandia at the beginning of the year.'

factual_claims.claim: Cruise passengers increased 47.8% due to 12 additional cruise calls and higher passenger capacity.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating Volumes section: 'By contrast, the number of cruise passengers increased by 32 thousand (+47.8%) as the number of cruise ship calls increased by 12 and the visiting ships had a higher combined passenger capacity.'

factual_claims.claim: Vessel calls decreased 4.8% to 3,376.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operating Volumes table: 'Number of vessel calls 3,376 (2026) vs 3,546 (2025)' with a 'Change %' of –4.8%.

factual_claims.claim: Comparability was negatively affected by the prior-year EUR 0.9 million profit from the sale of land for the Rail Baltica project and a EUR 0.9 million insurance indemnity related to Botnica repairs; neither benefited 2026.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management Report: 'The result for the comparative period was also positively affected by the profit from the disposal of land for the Rail Baltica project and the insurance indemnity received.' Note 12 footnote states EUR 900 thousand insurance indemnity received in 2025 for Botnica repairs.

factual_claims.claim: These factors, together with higher expenses and depreciation, outweighed revenue growth.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Management Report: 'The decline in operating profit was mainly attributable to higher operating expenses... Higher depreciation, amortisation and impairment along with higher personnel expenses also had a negative impact. The decline in operating profit was offset by revenue growth... The Group’s operating profit margin decreased...'

factual_claims.claim: Lower net finance costs, down 11.2% to EUR 2.3 million due to lower debt, partly moderated the decline in pre-tax profit.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Interim Condensed Consolidated Statement of Comprehensive Income: Finance costs, net for 2026 were EUR 2,279 thousand (2.279M) vs EUR 2,565 thousand (2025), an 11.2% decrease. Management Report: 'Net finance costs decreased by EUR 0.3 million (–11.2%) in the first 6 months of the year due to lower interest expense on loans and borrowings resulting from the lower level of debt.'

factual_claims.claim: The Group invested EUR 3.5 million, 70.6% less than a year earlier, while operating cash flow fell from EUR 26.3 million to EUR 18.2 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Investments section: 'In the first 6 months of 2026, the Group invested EUR 3.5 million, which is EUR 8.5 million less than in the same period last year.' Cash Flow Statement: Operating cash flow 18,151 (2026) vs 26,293 (2025).

factual_claims.claim: A EUR 19.2 million dividend was paid in May, equal to EUR 0.073 per share.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Dividends section: 'On 28 April 2026, the annual general meeting... approved the proposal... to distribute a dividend of EUR 0.073 per share and EUR 19.2 million in total... The dividends were paid out to the shareholders on 20 May 2026.'

factual_claims.claim: At period-end, net debt was EUR 145.8 million, up 1.5% year on year, and equity was EUR 367.7 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Interim Condensed Consolidated Statement of Financial Position: Net debt at 30 June 2026 was EUR 145,764 thousand (145.764M) vs EUR 143,664 thousand (143.664M) at 31 December 2025 – a 1.5% increase. Equity was EUR 367,677 thousand (367.677M).

factual_claims.claim: Management also identified risks from the US-Iran conflict, the Strait of Hormuz blockade, energy prices, and continuing effects of Russia’s war in Ukraine on liquid-bulk cargo flows.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Main Economic Risks section: 'The instability of the global economy due to the US-Iran conflict and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has led to increased fuel costs... Russia’s military activity in Ukraine has mainly affected the Group’s cargo business, resulting in a decreased share of liquid bulk.'

numerical_claims.label: CORRECT
numerical_claims.source_evidence: Note 11: Total revenue for 6 months 2026 is EUR 59,262 thousand (59.262M), representing a 2.4% increase from EUR 57,862 thousand (57.862M) in 2025.
